title: One Chaoshan Beef Cut Is Under 1% of the Cow — a 7-Second Dip | China Travel Expert
description:
In Chaoshan, beef hotpot is a science of seconds.

The prized "spoon-tendon" (匙柄) cut is the finest sliver of chuck — less than 1% of an entire cow. A whole cow yields only about 10 hotpot-worthy cuts, and each has its own exact dip time: spoon-tendon ~7 seconds, five-flower shin (五花趾) ~8 seconds, tenderloin ~5. Any longer and the texture is gone. The beef is never frozen — it's slaughtered and hand-sliced the same day.

🧭 Expert Tip: dip each slice in the plain clear broth first (that's the whole point), then the sha-cha sauce — and pull it the second it changes color.

潮汕牛肉火锅：一块匙柄不到全牛的1%，下锅只要7秒。
